title: CHAPTER 4: MEMORY AND FORGETTING
content:
👋 ሰላም ሰላም ውድ የEthioFresh ተማሪዎቻችን! እንደምን አላችሁ? ዛሬ ደግሞ የGeneral Psychology Chapter 4 ሁለተኛውንና የመጨረሻውን ክፍል (Part 2) ይዘንላችሁ መጥተናል። በዚህ ክፍል Forgetting (መርሳት) ምንድን ነው? ለምንስ እንረሳለን? አምስቱ የForgetting ቲዎሪዎች (Decay, Interference, Displacement, Motivated, Cue Dependent) እና አእምሯችንን እንዴት ማሻሻል እንደምንችል (Improving Memory) በስፋትና በጥልቀት እንመለከታለን። ቲዎሪዎች ፈተና ላይ ስለሚያዘወትሩ በደንብ ተከታተሉኝ። 👇👇👇


4.5. Forgetting

4.5.1 Meaning and Concepts of Forgetting
From the storehouse of information, most of us forget the names of individuals, names of places, and other information. In our daily living, we encounter so much information. If we attempted to encode, store, and recall all the information we face daily, we would be in trouble! Hence, we are selective in storing and forgetting information. Psychologists generally use the term forgetting to refer to the apparent loss of information already encoded and stored in long-term memory.

Hermann Ebbinghaus and the Forgetting Curve (1885/1913):
• The first systematic attempt to study forgetting was made by German psychologist Hermann Ebbinghaus using himself as his only subject.
• He memorized lists of three-letter nonsense syllables (meaningless sets of two consonants with a vowel in between, such as FIW and BOZ).
• By measuring how easy it was to relearn a given list of words after varying periods of time, he found that forgetting occurs systematically:
  1. Rapid Initial Decline: The most rapid forgetting occurs in the first hours, particularly in the very first hour after learning.
  2. Gradual Drop: After about nine hours, the rate of forgetting slows down and declines very little, even after the passage of many days.
  3. Relearning Advantage: Relearning previously mastered material is almost always faster than starting from scratch, whether the material is academic information or a motor skill (such as serving a tennis ball).

👉 የForgetting (የመርሳት) ትርጉም እና የEbbinghaus ጥናት :
• Forgetting (መርሳት): በሳይንሱ አገላለፅ ከዚህ ቀደም በደንብ Encode ተደረገው በLong-Term Memory (LTM) ውስጥ የተቀመጡ መረጃዎች በሂደት መጥፋት ወይም ማጣት ይባላል። እያንዳንዱን የምናየውንና የምንሰማውን ነገር እንዳንይዝ አእምሯችን መራጭ (Selective) መሆኑ ለእኛ ጥቅም ነው፤ ባይሆን ኖሮ አእምሯችን ይጨናነቅ ነበር!
• የEbbinghaus Forgetting Curve (የጀርመኑ ሳይንቲስት ጥናት): ሄርማን ኤቢንግሃውስ በራሱ ላይ ባደረገው ጥናት ትርጉም የሌላቸው ቃላትን (Nonsense Syllables - ለምሳሌ FIW, BOZ) በማጥናት መርሳት እንዴት እንደሚከሰት አጠና። የደረሰበት ዋና ውጤት፦
  1. መረሳት በጣም በከፍተኛ ፍጥነት የሚከሰተው በመጀመሪያው 1 ሰዓት ውስጥ ነው!
  2. ከ9 ሰዓት በኋላ ግን የመረሳቱ ፍጥነት ይቀንሳል (ይረጋል)።
  3. ከዚህ ቀደም የተማርነውን ነገር ደግሞ መለስ ብለን ለመማር (Relearning) ከዜሮ ከመጀመር ይልቅ በጣም ያነሰ ጊዜ ይወስድብናል።

💡 Exam Hint: ፈተና ላይ "According to Ebbinghaus, when does the most rapid rate of forgetting occur?" ከተባላችሁ መልሱ In the first hour immediately after learning የሚለው ነው! እንዲሁም Ebbinghaus የተጠቀመው Nonsense syllables መሆኑን አትርሱ።


4.6 Theories of Forgetting

Psychologists have proposed five distinct mechanisms/theories to account for why we forget information:

1. The Decay Theory:
• Holds that memory traces or engrams (actual physical changes in the brain) fade with time if they are not "accessed" now and then.
• In decay, the trace simply fades away with nothing left behind due to the passage of time.
• Decay occurs rapidly in Sensory Memory and Short-Term Memory (STM) unless rehearsed.
• Limitation: The mere passage of time does not account well for forgetting in Long-Term Memory (LTM). People commonly forget things that happened yesterday while remembering events from many years ago.

2. Interference Theory:
• Holds that forgetting occurs because similar items of information interfere with one another in either storage or retrieval. Information enters memory but gets confused with other information.
• Proactive Interference: Information learned earlier (old info) interferes with the recall of newer material.
• Retroactive Interference: New information interferes with the ability to remember older information.

3. Displacement Theory (New Memory for Old):
• Holds that new information entering memory can wipe out or displace old information, just as recording a new track over an audio/videotape will obliterate the original material.
• Key Note: This theory is mostly associated with Short-Term Memory (STM), where capacity is limited to 7 ± 2 chunks. It cannot be associated with LTM because LTM has virtually unlimited capacity.

4. Motivated Forgetting (Repression):
• Sigmund Freud maintained that people forget because they block from consciousness those memories that are too threatening, painful, or embarrassing to live with.
• Freud called this self-protective process Repression. Today, psychologists prefer the broader term Motivated Forgetting.

5. Cue-Dependent Forgetting:
• Occurs when we lack retrieval cues—items of information that help us find specific stored memories in LTM (like losing the call number for a book in the mind's library).
• Context-Dependent Memory: Remembering is easier when you are in the same physical environment where the event/learning occurred.
• State-Dependent Memory: Your internal physical or emotional state acts as a retrieval cue. For instance, being in the same emotional state (or physical state) during retrieval as during encoding helps recall.

👉 አምስቱ Forgetting ቲዎሪዎች :
• 1. Decay Theory (የጊዜ ብዛት/መደብዘዝ): መረጃው ሳይደጋገም ጊዜ እያለፈ ሲሄድ በአእምሯችን ውስጥ ያለው የነርቭ መስመር (Engram) እየደበዘዘ ይጠፋል። በተለይ በSensory እና STM ላይ ይሰራል።
• 2. Interference Theory (የመረጃዎች መደራረብ/መቀላቀል): ተመሳሳይም መረጃዎች እርስ በእርስ ሲቀላቀሉ ይከሰታል። በሁለት ይከፈላል፦
  - Proactive: አሮጌው መረጃ አዲሱን እንዳናስታውስ ሲከለክለን (ለምሳሌ፡ የድሮ ስልካችንን ቁጥር በማሰብ የአዲሱን ቁጥር መርሳት)።
  - Retroactive: አዲሱ መረጃ አሮጌውን እንዳናስታውስ ሲከለክለን (ለምሳሌ፡ የአዲሱን የክፍል አስተማሪ ስም አውቀን የድሮውን መርሳት)።
• 3. Displacement Theory (አዲሱ መረጃ አሮጌውን መግፋት): አዲስ መረጃ ሲመጣ አሮጌውን ገፍቶ ያወጣዋል (ልክ ካሴት ላይ አዲስ ድምፅ ስንቀዳ የድሮው እንደሚጠፋ)። ይህ የሚሆነው በShort-Term Memory (STM) ላይ ብቻ ነው፤ ምክንያቱም ቦታው मर्याደኛ (7±2) ስለሆነ!
• 4. Motivated Forgetting / Repression (በፍላጎት መርሳት): ሲግመንድ ፍሮይድ እንዳለው አእምሯችን የሚያሰቃዩ፣ የሚያሳፍሩ ወይም የሚያስፈሩ ትውስታዎችን ሆን ብሎ ወደ ያልነቃው አእምሮአችን (Unconscious) በመግፋት እንዲረሱ ያደርጋል።
• 5. Cue-Dependent Forgetting (የማስታወሻ ምልክት ማጣት): መረጃው LTM ውስጥ አለ ነገር ግን የሚጠቁመን መንገድ (Cue) ስላጣን ማስታወስ አንችልም። በሚጠናበት ወቅት የነበረው ቦታ (Context) ወይም ስሜት/አካላዊ ሁኔታ (State) ሲደገም ማስታወስ ይቻላል።

💡 Exam Hint: በፈተና ላይ "Proactive vs Retroactive" በጣም የሚጠየቅ ጥያቄ ነው! ቀላል ዘዴ፦ Pro = Old interferes with New፣ Retro = New interferes with Old ብላችሁ ያዙት! እንዲሁም Displacement Theory በLTM ላይ አይሰራም የሚለው የፈተና ትኩረት ነው።


4.7. Improving Memory

Someday, drugs may be available to help people with memory deficiencies. For the time being, however, we must rely on mental strategies and general guidelines to enhance learning and retention:

1. Pay Attention: We often fail to remember simply because we never encoded the information in the first place. Conscious focus ensures initial encoding.
2. Encode Information in More Than One Way: The more elaborate the encoding of information (visual, auditory, semantic), the more memorable it will be.
3. Add Meaning: The more meaningful the material, the more likely it is to link up with information already existing in Long-Term Memory.
4. Take Your Time (Rest & Sleep): Minimize interference by using study breaks for rest or recreation. Sleep is the ultimate way to reduce interference and consolidate memory traces.
5. Overlearn: Studying and practicing information even after you think you already know it is one of the best ways to ensure long-term retention.
6. Monitor Your Learning: Test yourself frequently, rehearse thoroughly, and review periodically to assess your mastery level.

👉 ትውስታችንን/አእምሯችንን ማሻሻያ 6 ዘዴዎች :
• 1. Pay Attention (ትኩረት መስጠት): አብዛኛውን ጊዜ የምንረሳው በደንብ ባለማጠናታችን ሳይሆን ከመጀመሪያውም ትኩረት ሰጥተን Encode ስላላደረግነው ነው!
• 2. Encode in Multiple Ways (በተለያዩ መንገዶች መቅረፅ): መረጃውን በጽሁፍ፣ በስዕልና በድምፅ አዳቅሎ ማናት ያጠናክረዋል።
• 3. Add Meaning (ትርጉም መስጠት): ይዘቱን ከምናውቀው የህይወት ልምድ ጋር በማያያዝ ማናት ረጅም ጊዜ እንዲቆይ ያደርገዋል።
• 4. Rest & Sleep (እረፍት እና እንቅልፍ): በእንቅልፍ ጊዜ አእምሯችን ያጠናነውን ነገር ያደራጃል (Consolidate ያደርጋል)፤ መደራረብንም ይከላከላል።
• 5. Overlearn (ደግሞ ደጋግሞ ማናት): አውቄዋለሁ ካልን በኋላም ቢሆን ደግሞ ደጋግሞ መለማመድ ትውስታችንን የማይጠፋ ያደርገዋል።
• 6. Monitor Learning (ራስን መፈተሽ): በየጊዜው ራስን መፈተሽና ከጓደኛ ጋር መከለስ ዝግጅታችንን ያጠናክራል።
